outcome: One software-defined storage pool that serves several network functions and scales by adding nodes instead of stranding capacity in silos.
overview: Telecom operators end up with storage silos because each network function arrived with its own array, its own performance requirement and its own refresh date, and capacity stranded in one silo cannot serve another however badly that other one needs it. PowerFlex separates storage from the arrays by pooling media across servers and serving it as software-defined block. Capacity and performance then scale with the nodes contributing to the pool rather than with an array’s controller pair, which is the property that suits a workload set growing unevenly. The design effort moves to the network fabric, because that is what becomes the limiting factor.

benefits.text: Capacity is pooled across servers rather than stranded in per-function arrays
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance data; a design built on invoice history or on projected growth alone produces a quotation rather than an architecture

benefits.text: Capacity and performance scale by adding nodes rather than by replacing a controller pair
benefits.limits: Scaling is linear within the design’s network fabric assumptions; the fabric becomes the constraint before the software does

benefits.text: One storage layer serves several network functions with different profiles
benefits.limits: Shared infrastructure means shared failure domains; the design must state which functions can tolerate that and which cannot

residency: Entirely on operator-owned equipment inside the operator’s data centres

notFor.situation: An estate already running a software-defined storage platform
notFor.why: Two software-defined layers means two failure domains and two operating models for one job

notFor.situation: A small estate with one workload profile
notFor.why: The value comes from serving several profiles from one pool; with one profile a conventional array is simpler

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Dell implementation partner · Duration: 12–16 weeks to a pool serving the first network functions, hardware lead time excluded
Support model: Vendor software and hardware support with a replacement term matched to network criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Assessment — per-silo capacity and performance, fabric review, vendor constraints
2) Design — pool layout, failure domains, fabric sizing and migration order
3) Build — nodes deployed, pool established, fabric validated under load
4) Migrate and hand over — functions migrated, silos decommissioned, operations handed over
deliverables: Measured pool performance under load meets the design figure with the fabric in place
Failure domain behaviour is demonstrated by test rather than described
Each migrated function has a dated decommission plan for the array it left
effort: 12–16 weeks to a pool serving the first network functions, hardware lead time excluded
